body:
## What does instant coffee jar mean for an Indian kitchen?

If you’ve ever opened an instant coffee jar and wondered what it really means for your kitchen, think of it as a shortcut that still lets you taste the real bean. At Purity Beans, the jars are simple: a 50‑gram packet of Bold pure coffee costs ₹239, while a 100‑gram pack is ₹369. The Purista gourmet Robusta comes in the same price band – ₹319 for 50g, ₹509 for 100g – and the Purica Arabica follows suit at ₹329 and ₹559 respectively. Ultra Blend, which is 70% coffee and 30% chicory, is a bit lighter at ₹209 for 50g and ₹309 for 100g. For a tasting flight, the Variety Box of four 50‑gram jars is ₹877, saving you ₹219 compared to buying each separately. A quick tip: start with a 50‑gram packet, brew a shot, and feel the difference before you decide the right size for your daily ritual.

### A plain definition

Whatever brought you here, the label settles it. The other single jars on this page are 0% chicory.

## How do you read the chicory line on the jar?

The ingredient list is the only line that matters. Turn the jar around and look for the word chicory — if it appears, the blend contains it; if it does not, you are holding pure coffee. Purity Beans prints that line in plain language so there is no guesswork. The other three — Bold at ₹239 for 50g and ₹369 for 100g, Purista at ₹319 for 50g and ₹509 for 100g, and Purica at ₹329 for 50g and ₹559 for 100g — all show zero chicory. A quick rule of thumb: if you drink your coffee black or want the full caffeine kick, reach for one of the zero-chicory jars. If you prefer a milder, milk-friendly cup with a softer caffeine lift, Ultra Blend is built for that. Pick the jar that matches how you actually drink coffee, not the one with the loudest label.

## Which jar suits the way you drink coffee?

Choosing from the Purity Beans lineup comes down to how you actually take your coffee. If you drink it black and want a serious morning kick, the 100g Bold at ₹369 is the workhorse — agglomerated granules that dissolve clean and deliver high caffeine without bitterness. When the priority is pure flavor clarity, the freeze-dried jars shine: Purica (100g, ₹559) brings caramel and chocolate notes that hold up in an americano, while Purista (100g, ₹509) offers a bold, crema-rich Robusta experience. A practical tip: start with the 50g sizes to learn your preference before committing to the larger jars. The Variety Box (4 × 50g, ₹877) lets you taste all four side by side for less than buying separately, so you discover your daily driver without guesswork.

## What does each jar cost in rupees?

Purity Beans prices each jar so you can match the coffee to the moment. Bold 50g is ₹239 and the 100g is ₹369 — a strong, agglomerated cup that wakes you up without any filler. Purista comes in at ₹319 for 50g and ₹509 for 100g; the freeze-dried Robusta granules hold a rich crema that feels special in a mid-afternoon mug. Purica, the freeze-dried Arabica, is ₹329 for 50g and ₹559 for 100g, delivering caramel and chocolate notes that shine black or in a dessert. Prima is pure Arabica agglomerated at ₹269 and ₹449, though it is not the freeze-dried gourmet line. If you are deciding between processes, remember: freeze-dried means Purica and Purista only. A practical tip: grab the 50g size first when you are trying a new roast profile.

## How do people brew instant coffee in Indian cities?

In most Indian city kitchens, instant coffee starts with a kettle or a microwave mug. Some pour hot water straight over the granules and stir; others swear by the 'bloom' method — a splash of hot water first, a quick swirl, then the rest of the cup. Milk drinkers often heat milk on the stove, froth it with a small whisk, and fold in the coffee at the end. A friend in Bangalore keeps a French press on her desk and uses it for instant on busy mornings — she says the plunge gives a silkier mouthfeel. If you like it black, try dissolving the granules in a teaspoon of room-temperature water before adding hot water; it prevents clumping and brings out more aroma. Purity Beans makes four jars for these rituals. Bold is agglomerated pure coffee with a deep, full body at ₹239 for 50g and ₹369 for 100g. Purista and Purica are freeze-dried — Robusta at ₹319 and ₹509, Arabica at ₹329 and ₹559 — both zero chicory.

## How do you choose a jar without a slogan?

Start with how you drink it. If your morning ritual is a strong black cup that wakes you up properly, Bold (₹369 for 100g) is built for that — agglomerated granules, pure coffee, zero chicory. If you prefer milk and want something smooth for everyday sipping, Ultra Blend (₹309 for 100g) gives you 70 percent coffee and 30 percent chicory at a gentle price. For the weekends when you want cafe-style flavor without leaving home, Purica (₹559 for 100g) brings freeze-dried Arabica with natural caramel notes, while Purista (₹509 for 100g) delivers freeze-dried Robusta with a rich crema. Can't decide? The Variety Box (₹877 for four 50g jars) lets you taste all four side by side. One practical tip: buy a 50g jar first when trying a new blend; it costs less than two cafe visits and tells you everything you need to know.
